To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the system has a unique traveling wave solution that connects the two constant equilibrium states; (2) there is a unique traveling wave connecting the two constant equilibrium state; (3) the wave sequence is unique; (4) the wave sequence consists of a rarefaction wave, a contact discontinuity, and a shock wave; and (5) the shock wave is a strong shock wave.
(i) there are three traveling waves, one of them is monotone and the other two are non-monotone and (ii) the Riemann solutions are composed of the three waves.
the system admits combustion wave solutions and that the Riemann solution is comprised of rarefaction wave, contact discontinuity, and combustion wave.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the existence of traveling wave solutions and Riemann solution for a system of partial differential equations which models combustion of light, porous foam.
the mathematical analysis of a system of three partial differential equations that describes the dynamics of combustion in light porous foam, and the corresponding Riemann problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system under consideration is well-posed in the large.

, in the context of the present model, the existence of combustion waves is guaranteed by the presence of the heat source, and the existence of Riemann solutions is guaranteed by the fact that the heat source is not strong enough to make the wave speed supercritical.
the Riemann problem for the system of three partial differential equations modeling combustion of light porous foams is solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show the existence of traveling wave solutions for a model that describes combustion of light porous foams.
, for the first time, we have established a mathematical framework that allows us to rigorously analyze combustion of a light porous foam under a wide range of conditions.
we have shown that combustion waves exist, and that the waves are stable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of gravity, there are two types of waves, one that is a rarefaction wave and the other a contact discontinuity.
, despite the presence of two distinct reaction zones, the Riemann solution is not more complicated than the solution of the classical porous media equation.
the system is well posed in the sense of Hadamard.
